questions.statement: Which sentence correctly reports the question 'Do you speak Spanish'.
questions.context: A student repeats a classmate's question in a written report.

options.text: She asked if I spoke Spanish.
options.feedback: Correct. Reported yes or no questions use if and backshift the verb, so speak becomes spoke.

options.text: She asked if I speak Spanish.
options.feedback: The verb is not backshifted: in reported speech the present speak must become the past spoke.

options.text: She asked did I speak Spanish.
options.feedback: The auxiliary did is kept, but reported questions drop do, does and did completely.

options.text: She asked if did I speak Spanish.
options.feedback: If already marks the reported question, so the auxiliary did cannot also introduce it.

questions.explanation:
In reported yes or no questions, if or whether replaces the direct question, the auxiliary do disappears and the verb shifts one tense back.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly reports the question 'Where does she work'.
questions.context: A journalist writes down a question that a witness asked earlier.

options.text: He asked where did she work.
options.feedback: In reported questions the auxiliary did must be removed, not placed before the subject.

options.text: He asked where she worked.
options.feedback: Correct. The wh-word keeps its place, the auxiliary does is dropped and work becomes worked.

options.text: He asked where does she work.
options.feedback: The present does is not backshifted and also keeps the wrong auxiliary.

options.text: He asked where she works.
options.feedback: The verb stays in the present, but reported speech needs the past worked.

questions.explanation:
A reported wh-question keeps the question word but returns to normal word order, so does is dropped and the verb is backshifted.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly reports the command 'Close the window'.
questions.context: A teacher repeats an instruction that was given in class.

options.text: The teacher told us close the window.
options.feedback: The verb close needs to before it, because told is followed by object and to-infinitive.

options.text: The teacher said us to close the window.
options.feedback: The verb say cannot take a person as its object; use told us.

options.text: The teacher told us to close the window.
options.feedback: Correct. Reported commands use tell plus an object and a to-infinitive.

options.text: The teacher asked us close the window.
options.feedback: Asked us close lacks to, and asked usually reports a request rather than an order.

questions.explanation:
An affirmative command becomes tell plus object plus to plus the base verb, so Close the window turns into told us to close the window.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly reports the negative command 'Do not touch the wires'.
questions.context: A safety officer repeats a warning that was written on a sign.

options.text: She told him to not touch the wires.
options.feedback: Splitting the infinitive as to not touch is less standard than not to touch.

options.text: She said him not to touch the wires.
options.feedback: The verb say cannot take the object him; the correct reporting verb is told.

options.text: She told him do not touch the wires.
options.feedback: The direct form do not cannot survive inside a reported command.

options.text: She told him not to touch the wires.
options.feedback: Correct. A negative command uses not before the to-infinitive: not to touch.

questions.explanation:
Negative commands are reported with tell plus object plus not to plus the base verb, placing not before the infinitive.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly reports the question 'Why are you late'.
questions.context: A manager reports an employee's question to the rest of the team.

options.text: He asked why I was late.
options.feedback: Correct. The subject comes before the verb and are is backshifted to was.

options.text: He asked why was I late.
options.feedback: The inversion was I is the direct question order, not the reported order.

options.text: He asked why I were late.
options.feedback: The pronoun I takes was, never were, in the past tense.

options.text: He asked why am I late.
options.feedback: The present am is not backshifted and keeps the direct question word order.

questions.explanation:
A reported wh-question uses statement order, subject before verb, and backshifts the present are into the past was.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly reports the question 'Do you need help'.
questions.context: A nurse repeats a patient's question to the doctor.

options.text: She asked whether did I need help.
options.feedback: The auxiliary did must be dropped in a reported question with whether.

options.text: She asked whether I needed help.
options.feedback: Correct. Whether introduces the reported question and need is backshifted to needed.

options.text: She asked whether I need help.
options.feedback: The present need is not backshifted; the reported form is needed.

options.text: She asked whether do I need help.
options.feedback: The present do is kept and inverts the subject, which reported speech forbids.

questions.explanation:
Yes or no questions can be reported with whether; the auxiliary disappears and the verb moves one tense back.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly reports the request 'Please sit down'.
questions.context: A visitor repeats a polite request that a receptionist made.

options.text: He asked me sit down.
options.feedback: The verb sit needs to before it after asked me.

options.text: He said me to sit down.
options.feedback: The verb say cannot take me as an object; the reporting verb is asked.

options.text: He asked me to sit down.
options.feedback: Correct. A reported request uses ask plus object plus to-infinitive.

options.text: He asked to me sit down.
options.feedback: The preposition to cannot come before me in this structure.

questions.explanation:
Polite requests are reported with ask plus object plus to plus the base verb, so Please sit down becomes asked me to sit down.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly reports the question 'Can you help me'.
questions.context: A student reports a classmate's question about a favour.

options.text: She asked if I can help her.
options.feedback: The present can is not backshifted; the reported modal is could.

options.text: She asked if could I help her.
options.feedback: The modal could cannot invert with I in a reported if-clause.

options.text: She asked if I can help me.
options.feedback: The pronoun me is not changed to the third person her.

options.text: She asked if I could help her.
options.feedback: Correct. Can is backshifted to could and the first person me changes to her.

questions.explanation:
Reporting a question with can backshifts the modal to could and changes the speaker's pronoun me to her.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly reports the negative command 'Do not be late'.
questions.context: A coach repeats a negative instruction to a player.

options.text: He told me not to be late.
options.feedback: Correct. The negative command becomes not to be, with not before the infinitive.

options.text: He told me to do not be late.
options.feedback: The direct words do not cannot stay inside the reported infinitive.

options.text: He said me not to be late.
options.feedback: The verb said cannot take me as its object; use told me.

options.text: He told me do not be late.
options.feedback: The base command do not be cannot follow told without the to-infinitive.

questions.explanation:
A negative command is reported with tell plus object plus not to plus the base verb, so Do not be late becomes not to be late.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly reports the question 'Where do they live'.
questions.context: A tour guide reports a question that tourists asked at the desk.

options.text: She asked where did they live.
options.feedback: The auxiliary did keeps the direct question order, which reported speech removes.

options.text: She asked where they lived.
options.feedback: Correct. The auxiliary do is dropped and live is backshifted to lived.

options.text: She asked where do they live.
options.feedback: The present do is kept and the verb is not backshifted.

options.text: She asked where they live.
options.feedback: The verb stays present, but the reported form needs the past lived.

questions.explanation:
In a reported wh-question the auxiliary do disappears and the verb moves to the past, so do they live becomes they lived.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly reports the question 'What time does the train leave'.
questions.context: A passenger repeats a question about a timetable.

options.text: He asked what time did the train leave.
options.feedback: The auxiliary did creates a direct question order that reported speech does not allow.

options.text: He asked what time does the train leave.
options.feedback: The present does is kept instead of being dropped and backshifted.

options.text: He asked what time the train left.
options.feedback: Correct. The auxiliary does is dropped and leave is backshifted to left.

options.text: He asked what time the train leaves.
options.feedback: The verb leaves stays present, but the reported form is the past left.

questions.explanation:
After the question word, the reported clause uses subject then verb, drops does and shifts leave to left.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly reports the question 'Have you finished your homework'.
questions.context: A mother repeats a question her son asked about school.

options.text: She asked if have I finished my homework.
options.feedback: The auxiliary have cannot invert with I in a reported if-clause.

options.text: She asked if I have finished my homework.
options.feedback: The present perfect is not backshifted to the past perfect.

options.text: She asked if had I finished my homework.
options.feedback: The auxiliary had cannot invert with the subject in a reported clause.

options.text: She asked if I had finished my homework.
options.feedback: Correct. The present perfect have finished is backshifted to had finished.

questions.explanation:
When a present perfect question is reported, have finished shifts back to had finished and the subject keeps its normal position.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly reports the question 'Will you come to the party'.
questions.context: A friend repeats a question about a future plan.

options.text: He asked if I would come to the party.
options.feedback: Correct. Will is backshifted to would and the subject keeps its place after if.

options.text: He asked if I will come to the party.
options.feedback: The present will is not backshifted; the reported modal is would.

options.text: He asked if would I come to the party.
options.feedback: The modal would cannot invert with I in a reported if-clause.

options.text: He asked if I come to the party.
options.feedback: The base verb come has lost the future meaning that would carries.

questions.explanation:
A reported question with will changes the modal to would and keeps the statement order after if.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly reports the command 'Open your books and read page ten'.
questions.context: A pupil reports a two-part instruction from a teacher.

options.text: The teacher told the class open their books and read page ten.
options.feedback: The first verb open needs to before it after told the class.

options.text: The teacher told the class to open their books and read page ten.
options.feedback: Correct. Both verbs share one to-infinitive: to open and read.

options.text: The teacher said the class to open their books and read page ten.
options.feedback: The verb said cannot take the class as its object; use told.

options.text: The teacher told the class to opening their books and read page ten.
options.feedback: The infinitive is to open, not to opening, because no gerund is used here.

questions.explanation:
When a command has two actions, tell plus object plus to plus base verb covers both, so to open and read is correct.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly reports the question 'Why didn't you call me'.
questions.context: A woman repeats a question about a missed phone call.

options.text: She asked why didn't I call her.
options.feedback: The auxiliary didn't keeps the direct question inversion, which reported speech removes.

options.text: She asked why I didn't called her.
options.feedback: The auxiliary didn't already marks the past, so call must stay in the base form.

options.text: She asked why I hadn't called her.
options.feedback: Correct. The past simple negative is backshifted to the past perfect hadn't called.

options.text: She asked why hadn't I called her.
options.feedback: The auxiliary hadn't cannot invert with I inside a reported clause.

questions.explanation:
A past simple question is reported with the past perfect, so didn't call becomes hadn't called in statement order.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly reports the negative command 'Do not open the door for strangers'.
questions.context: A parent repeats a safety rule given to a child.

options.text: They told the child to not open the door for strangers.
options.feedback: The split form to not open is less standard than the usual not to open.

options.text: They said the child not to open the door for strangers.
options.feedback: The verb said cannot take the child as its object; the reporting verb is told.

options.text: They told the child do not open the door for strangers.
options.feedback: The direct imperative do not open cannot stay inside a reported command.

options.text: They told the child not to open the door for strangers.
options.feedback: Correct. The negative infinitive is not to open, placed after the object.

questions.explanation:
The negative command keeps the order tell plus object plus not to plus base verb, so the sign becomes not to open.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly reports the question 'Do you know where she is'.
questions.context: A detective repeats a question that a witness had already reported.

options.text: He asked if I knew where she was.
options.feedback: Correct. The main verb know backshifts to knew and the embedded clause keeps she was.

options.text: He asked if I knew where was she.
options.feedback: The embedded clause where she is keeps statement order, so was she is wrong.

options.text: He asked did I know where she was.
options.feedback: The auxiliary did must be dropped after the reporting verb asked.

options.text: He asked if did I know where she was.
options.feedback: If and the auxiliary did cannot both introduce the same reported question.

questions.explanation:
When a yes or no question contains another clause, both verbs backshift and neither keeps the direct question order.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly reports the command 'Tell me what you want'.
questions.context: A secretary reports an instruction that was given at a meeting.

options.text: She told me tell her what I wanted.
options.feedback: The verb tell needs to before it after told me.

options.text: She told me to tell her what I wanted.
options.feedback: Correct. The command uses to tell and the embedded verb want is backshifted to wanted.

options.text: She said me to tell her what I wanted.
options.feedback: The verb said cannot take me as an object; use told me.

options.text: She told me to tell her what I want.
options.feedback: The embedded present want is not backshifted to the past wanted.

questions.explanation:
A command that contains another clause takes tell plus object plus to plus base verb, and the inner verb also shifts back.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly reports the question 'Do they sell tickets here'.
questions.context: A traveller repeats a question about tickets at the station.

options.text: He asked whether did they sell tickets there.
options.feedback: The auxiliary did is kept and inverts the subject, which reported speech forbids.

options.text: He asked whether they sell tickets here.
options.feedback: The present sell and the place here are both left unchanged.

options.text: He asked whether they sold tickets there.
options.feedback: Correct. Whether replaces the question, sell backshifts to sold and here becomes there.

options.text: He asked whether do they sell tickets here.
options.feedback: The auxiliary do is kept and here is not changed to there.

questions.explanation:
A reported yes or no question uses whether, drops do, backshifts sell to sold and changes here to there.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly reports the command 'Give me the keys'.
questions.context: A guard repeats an order that a driver gave to a colleague.

options.text: He told her give him the keys.
options.feedback: The verb give needs to before it after told her.

options.text: He said her to give him the keys.
options.feedback: The verb said cannot take her as its object; use told her.

options.text: He told her to give me the keys.
options.feedback: The pronoun me is not changed to the third person him in reported speech.

options.text: He told her to give him the keys.
options.feedback: Correct. The imperative becomes to give and the first person me changes to him.

questions.explanation:
In a reported command the imperative becomes a to-infinitive and the speaker's pronoun me changes to him.
---
questions.subject: ingles
